claim.quote: We report on the first production of an antihydrogen beam by charge exchange of 6.1 keV antiprotons with a cloud of positronium in the GBAR experiment at CERN.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal version is Eur. Phys. J. C 83, 1004 (2023) per the arXiv DOI.

key_value_text.quote: We observe an excess over background indicating antihydrogen production with a significance of 3-4 standard deviations.
key_value_text.value: Excess over background indicating antihydrogen production at 3-4 standard deviations

name: Production of antihydrogen atoms by 6 keV antiprotons through a positronium cloud

significance.note: Reported by the collaboration as "3-4 standard deviations", below the five-sigma convention for an observation; labelled a technology milestone, not a discovery.
significance.quote: We observe an excess over background indicating antihydrogen production with a significance of 3-4 standard deviations.

summary.plain: GBAR reported its first antihydrogen: antiprotons from CERN’s ELENA ring were sent through a cloud of positronium atoms. The excess over background indicates antihydrogen production at a significance of 3 to 4 standard deviations.
summary.technical: First production of an antihydrogen beam by charge exchange of 6.1 keV antiprotons delivered by AD/ELENA with a positronium cloud made from a linac-driven positron beam; an excess over background indicates production with a significance of 3-4 standard deviations.

title: Production of antihydrogen atoms by 6 keV antiprotons through a positronium cloud
why_it_matters: This is the first step of the GBAR scheme, which will go on to antihydrogen ions and a free-fall measurement; the CERN news item states the aim of testing the equivalence principle with antimatter.
